guidelines.title: consistent not uniform
guidelines.rule: Consistent, not uniform — same behaviour for common components; services may apply their own colour, type, sub-logo, and flows without disrupting the shared default.
pass_when: Shared components keep the same behaviour; service colour/type/sub-logo/flow differences do not change that default behaviour.
fail_when: A service restyles a common control so its behaviour no longer matches the shared default.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Visual loudness / one-primary as this principle; a house brand-token set.

guidelines.title: visual loudness primary secondary tertiary
guidelines.rule: Visual loudness is a named three-level scale: primary / secondary / tertiary so designers can balance visual priority. Dual-cite Actions one-primary; this row is the three-loudness scale, not a second “one primary” rule.
pass_when: Button variants on a view map to primary / secondary / tertiary loudness; one primary remains the dual-cite cap.
fail_when: All actions share the same loudness with no primary/secondary/tertiary distinction, claimed as this GOLD scale.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Actions one-primary as this three-level row; Next vs Save-progress pairing as this scale.

guidelines.title: next primary save progress secondary
guidelines.rule: Multi-page pairing: Next page is primary; Save progress is secondary.
pass_when: On a multi-page form, Next page is the primary control and Save progress is secondary.
fail_when: Save progress is styled as primary, or Next page is demoted below Save progress.
guidelines.do_not_claim: The three-loudness scale as this pairing; NL last-step-is-send as this GOLD Next/Save pair.

guidelines.title: avoid select except long lists
guidelines.rule: Avoid select except long lists — selects hide content, are inconsistent across devices, and are hard for low digital literacy. Small lists (e.g. Australian state/territory) → radios / checkboxes / text. Long lists (e.g. country) may trade usability for compactness. Dual-cite GOV.UK / USWDS / NSW cutoffs; no house number.
pass_when: Short lists use radios/checkboxes/text; select is reserved for long lists (e.g. country). Dual-cite cutoff schools are not collapsed into a house N.
fail_when: A short list (e.g. state/territory) is a select; or a house numeric cutoff is invented as GOLD.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A house “use select above N options”; NL `<select multiple>` ban as this single-select usage row.

guidelines.title: progress indicator out of order returnable
guidelines.rule: Progress indicator is for out-of-order, returnable tasks (tax return / driver’s licence). Named states: `todo` / `doing` / `done`. Dual-cite USWDS linear step indicator and GOV.UK “test without a progress indicator”; do not collapse into one progress widget.
pass_when: Non-linear returnable tasks use the GOLD indicator with todo/doing/done; linear wizards are not forced into this widget (USWDS linear / GOV.UK test-without remain dual-cites).
fail_when: A linear one-way wizard is this GOLD out-of-order indicator, or todo/doing/done is collapsed with USWDS linear / GOV.UK no-indicator into one house widget.
guidelines.do_not_claim: USWDS linear step indicator or GOV.UK test-without as this GOLD row; NL step n of m in `document.title`.

guidelines.title: search placement home vs results
guidelines.rule: Search placement — landing/home: top-right (where people expect it). Results page: search box closer to the results so query and hits read as related. Dual-cite USWDS persist-query / homepage-is-a-box.
pass_when: Home search is top-right; results-page search sits close to the hits.
fail_when: Home search is not where people expect (top-right); results-page search is far from the hits.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Search input attributes (autocomplete/spellcheck) as this placement row; USWDS persist-query as a merge.

guidelines.title: search input attributes
guidelines.rule: Search input attributes — `autocomplete` on search can leak sensitive queries on shared machines. `autocorrect` / `spellcheck` conflict with server-side search correction. Do not rely on `required` as the only “empty search” message.
pass_when: Search does not use `autocomplete` in a way that stores sensitive queries; `autocorrect`/`spellcheck` are not fighting server-side correction; empty search is not messaged by `required` alone.
fail_when: Search `autocomplete` stores queries on a shared machine; `required` is the only empty-search message.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Header-search placeholder exception; Suomi visually-hidden search label as this attributes row.

guidelines.title: card one inner link hit area
guidelines.rule: Card: one inner link; hit-area wraps the card. Do not wrap the whole card in `<a>` (screen readers announce the entire contents; the links landmark becomes unusable). Keep a large click target via CSS hit-area on a single inner anchor. Dual-cite USWDS “card is an action, not a frame.”
pass_when: One inner `<a>`; CSS hit-area makes the card clickable; the card itself is not the `<a>`.
fail_when: The whole card is wrapped in `<a>`, or multiple competing links sit in the card without a single inner-anchor pattern.
guidelines.do_not_claim: USWDS “card is an action” as a merge that drops the inner-anchor + landmark fail.

guidelines.title: accordion find in page misses collapsed
guidelines.rule: Accordion: hidden copy is invisible to Find in page — browsers’ find does not match collapsed accordion text. Dual-cite USWDS “use only if users need a few pieces”; this names the find-in-page failure.
pass_when: Content people must find with Find in page is not only inside a collapsed accordion.
fail_when: Essential copy lives only in collapsed accordion panels (Find in page cannot match it).
guidelines.do_not_claim: USWDS accordion-sparingly as a merge that drops the find-in-page name.

guidelines.title: no abbr expand on first mention
guidelines.rule: Don’t use `<abbr>`; expand on first mention. Screen-reader support for `<abbr>` is limited. Write “Australian Football League (AFL)” then “AFL”. Dual-cite Canada abbreviations (widest-audience test); GOLD names the element ban + first-mention pattern.
pass_when: First mention is expanded with the short form in parentheses; later mentions use the short form; no `<abbr>`.
fail_when: `<abbr>` is used, or the short form appears first with no expansion.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Canada widest-audience abbreviations as a merge that drops the `<abbr>` ban.
